name: Grounding of clinical text in its source
description: Ties every claim and figure in a model's clinical output to the source it was read from, and catches required items left out.
limits: A quote shows where a claim came from, not that the claim follows from it: a clinician still reads the output. Figures are matched by value and unit, not by meaning. Rates published for this pack come from a labelled set; until the clinical safety lead labels one, the set in the reference agent is synthetic and says so.

hazards.title: A summary states something the source does not (hallucination) and a clinician acts on it
A summary leaves out a required item (an allergy, a medication)

controls.title: Every claim is quoted from the source
controls.requirement: Each claim in the output carries a quote found word for word in the source, outside any instruction-like text the source contains.

controls.title: Every figure appears in the source
controls.requirement: Each figure in the output, with its unit when it has one, appears in the source.

controls.title: Required items are not omitted
controls.requirement: Each required item is present, or recorded as none only where the source says so.

controls.title: Wrongful rejection of good text is measured
controls.requirement: The share of correct outputs these checks reject is measured on a labelled set and stays under the agreed limit.
